clue.text: Figure captivated by performing artist — rope tricks are his speciality

indicators.note: being captivated by something is being held inside it, so the figure sits within the other letters
performing suggests the letters are put through their paces and rearranged

parts.note: a digit is a numerical figure

explanation.surface: A conjuror whose speciality is the Indian rope trick, held up as a figure who wows audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rope' seems to belong with 'tricks' as the Indian rope trick, but it is fodder for 'performing'; 'captivated by' puts the figure inside the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror, whose sleight of hand is his stock in trade, is a man for whom tricks are the specialism.

clue.text: Debt taken on by football club, not Real

indicators.note: a debt taken on by a club is absorbed into it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: A football club runs up debts, unlike the grand Spanish club Real Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real' looks like Real Madrid, the Spanish football club, but in the definition it simply means genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something counterfeit or false is not genuine, which is the plain meaning of not real.

clue.text: Crazy like …

definitions.meaning: an ellipsis is a row of dots, so something like it is covered in dots

explanation.surface: The clue trails off into the next one, as if lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: The three dots also lead into the next clue, which begins with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is a sense of the word, and resembling a row of dots is the literal second meaning.

clue.text: … one Greek character constrained by measures

indicators.note: something constrained by measures is held within them, so these letters go inside

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length
I is the Roman numeral one
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a single Greek letter is hemmed in by units of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the three dots themselves, the punctuation mark joining this clue to the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: Three dots in a row are the punctuation mark showing an omission or a trailing off.

clue.text: Port's excessive consumption close to binge — idiot's thrown up

parts.note: OD is an overdose, taking too much of something

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
in a down clue, thrown up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ass is an idiot; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: A drinking binge in a port ends with a fool being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown up' looks like vomiting after the binge, but in this down clue it turns the idiot upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea seaport in Ukraine.

clue.text: Page comes back with gold for herald

parts.note: something that recurs happens again
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A page boy returns carrying gold for a herald at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner announcing what is to come is a harbinger, so herald is a synonym.

clue.text: Open out list containing Ban Ki-moon's name?

parts.note: Ban Ki-moon was Secretary-General of the United Nations, so the UN is the name attached to him
a roll is a list of names

explanation.surface: Someone unfurls a register looking for the name of the former UN chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is a UN roll: a list of United Nations staff, which would contain Ban Ki-moon's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread out something rolled up, such as a scroll or carpet, is to open it out flat.

clue.text: Will they make smut, rude bits, blue gags, even some vile oath that isn't very nice?

definitions.text: Will they make smut, rude bits, blue gags, even some vile oath that isn't very nice?

parts.words: Will they make smut, rude bits, blue gags, even some vile oath that isn't very nice?
parts.note: every word of this clue has exactly four letters, and swear words are proverbially words of that length

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether crude language is what produces filth, dirty jokes and nasty oaths.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself is built entirely of four-letter words, so it describes its own construction as well as obscenities.
explanation.definitionFit: Swear words are traditionally called this because so many English obscenities are short, rude terms of that length.

clue.text: After theological study, fidgety pope was first to get settled again

indicators.note: after the first piece, so the other pieces follow it in order

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject

indicators.note: fidgety means restless, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: After studying theology, a restless pope took the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To populate a place a second time is to resettle it with inhabitants.

clue.text: Republican Party keeps playing some classical music

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a do is a party
on means being performed or playing

explanation.surface: A Republican Party event features classical music being played.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form with a recurring theme, often the last movement of a classical sonata.

clue.text: Tritest Brahms and Liszt passages from fugues

indicators.note: rhyming slang for drunk, so the letters reel about and are rearranged

explanation.surface: The most clichéd parts of fugues by two Romantic composers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is Cockney rhyming slang for 'pissed', meaning drunk, which signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fugue, overlapping entries of the subject are each called a stretto; the plural is the Italian form.

clue.text: Relief from outspoken fool

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is one that sounds the same

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: An outspoken fool, of all people, offers some relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Help or comfort in time of trouble is aid and assistance, a synonym of relief.

clue.text: Promise made by Liberal, one that could be false?

parts.note: 'I do' is the promise made in a wedding ceremony

explanation.surface: A Liberal makes a promise that may turn out to be untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' looks like a broken promise, but the definition alludes to a false idol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible warns against false gods worshipped as images, hence the phrase and the question mark.

clue.text: Heading for Egyptian resort, bore acquires eastern footwear

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
to drill is to bore a hole

explanation.surface: Someone heads for an Egyptian resort, where a bore buys oriental shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas shoe with a rope sole is a type of footwear, originally from the Pyrenees.

clue.text: Activity in the City gets you skint? Then see red!

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money
to see red is to rage with anger

explanation.surface: Working in finance leaves you penniless, and then you get angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing in shares on behalf of clients is a typical business carried on in London's financial district.

clue.text: Disheartened topless siren ordered implants

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order
with its heart removed only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A topless siren, feeling low, has had breast implants fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' looks like sad, but empties TOPLESS to TS; 'ordered' then rearranges TS with SIREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Things put into something else are insertions, as a surgeon puts implants in; both are plural nouns.

clue.text: Person regularly sulks about hotel — is it Sibyl?

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word
about means going round, so these letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone moping around a hotel is perhaps Sybil, the fiery hotel owner's wife of television sitcom fame.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Sybil Fawlty of the TV sitcom Fawlty Towers, but the sibyl of ancient myth was a female seer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a woman of classical antiquity who foretold the future, an example of a seer.

clue.text: Head of army in favour of donning long dress

indicators.note: to don something is to put it on, so these letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: to pine is to long for something

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: for means in favour of

explanation.surface: An army chief is keen on wearing a long dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like the length of the dress, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless apron-like garment worn over a blouse is a type of dress.

clue.text: In conversation, loftier Greek is suitable for priests

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so the word is one that sounds alike

parts.note: higher means loftier and Attic is the Greek of Athens

explanation.surface: In talk, a more elevated form of Greek is suited to the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things relating to priests, especially the ancient Egyptian priestly script.

clue.text: Sliding discipline is besetting church racing to get rid of rector

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so these letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it from the word

parts.note: karting is racing in go-karts

explanation.surface: A church gripped by motor racing wants rid of its vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding on blades over a frozen rink is a sport, a discipline of the Winter Olympics.

clue.text: Wit from Rabelais, mischievous creature sending up English

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a letter up moves it towards the top

parts.note: a sprite is an elf or fairy

explanation.surface: The French author's humour comes from an impish creature lampooning the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending up' looks like mockery, but it moves the E of SPRITE to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for liveliness of mind, a word Rabelais would use, means wit.

clue.text: Ploughman's lunch for a starter eaten by workman

indicators.note: something eaten by another goes inside it

parts.note: a tiler is a workman who lays tiles

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A workman eats a ploughman's lunch, the British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle, as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a pub meal of bread and cheese; the definition is only 'Ploughman'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tills the soil, turning the land with a plough, is a farm worker.

clue.text: RIP — a sign of mourning

definitions.meaning: to rip is to rend, as cloth
a drop from the eye shed in grief

explanation.surface: The epitaph Rest In Peace on a gravestone, a mark of grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'RIP' looks like the epitaph Rest In Peace, but it is the verb rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip in fabric is a rent, and a drop of salt water from the eye shows grief; the two senses differ in sound.

clue.text: French vote for elevated, divine female

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the word is read upwards

parts.note: aye is a vote in favour

explanation.surface: French voting for a lofty goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse goddess of love and fertility is a female deity.

clue.text: Clobber soldiers going into shock

indicators.note: the soldiers enter the other word, so their letters go inside

parts.note: to appal is to shock
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone attacks soldiers who are in a state of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb meaning beat, but it is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for one's gear or clothing is a synonym of garments.

clue.text: Jazzy piece follows considerably old medley

indicators.note: the jazz piece comes after the word for considerably

parts.note: far means by a great deal, as in far better
a rag is a ragtime piece

explanation.surface: A jazz number comes after a much older mixture of tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused jumble of things is a hotchpotch, so medley is a synonym.

clue.text: Where footballer may play with ball is not yet settled

parts.note: O is a ball from its round shape
a winger plays on the wing of the pitch

explanation.surface: A footballer's position and the ball, though the matter remains unresolved.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still outstanding is unpaid, that is not yet settled.

clue.text: Noble woman embracing unknown, who won't linger in bed

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so these letters surround the other piece

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
bird is British slang for a woman
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady clasps a stranger, someone who rises early.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises at dawn is an early riser, from the proverb about catching the worm.
